newsitem.title: EGYPT: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - June 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - June 1.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian economic press this week. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-BORSA
- International financial institutions in joint local ventures in Egypt for first time.
- New stock exchange board issues first decrees to develop and improve trading.
- Head of National Company for Iron and Steel welcomes tariffs imposed by supplies minister to prevent dumping.
- Medinet Nasr Housing and Development buys 90 percent of Nasr Public Utilities and Installation for 36 million pounds ($10.60 million).
- Share offer in Egyptian Kuwaiti Holding Company closes in Egypt and Kuwait; applicants will receive 28.46 percent of shares they applied for. Three million shares were offered at $10 each.

-- Kima/Egyptian Chemical Industries after-tax net profit for first nine months of 1996/97 up 10.23 percent to 18.59 million from 16.14 million in same year ago period. Net sales down to 93.79 million pounds from 96.44 million.

-- Nasr Dehydrated Agricultural Products pre-tax net profit down to 2.38 million pounds from 4.5 million in first ten months of financial year. Sales also down to 11.8 million from 18.7 million for same period.
-- Egyptian Amercian Bank net profit for financial year that ended in 1996 up by 9.44 percent to 90.551 million pounds from 82.738 million in same year ago period.
- Export Development Bank of Egypt after-tax net profit for first nine months up 138.8 percent to 66.46 million pounds from 28.83 million.
-- Holding Company for Housing and Construction privatising Shams Housing and Development by offering investors at least 1.4 million shares or 10 percent in company.

-- Commercial International Bank gives out lower dividend for second year in a row. Annual general meeting decides to give out two pounds per share, compared to equivalent of 3.11 pounds per share last year.

-- Eighty percent of total shares of Nubareya Agricultural Engineering sold to public last week. Applicants will receive 5.34 percent of shares they applied for. It is the first privatisation by Holding Company for Agricultural Development. Holding company had originally offered just 300,000 shares for sale, or 30 percent of total, but increased it to 800,000 after strong interest.

-- Credit Foncier Egyptien bond offer closed on Thursday oversubscribed. Applicants expected to receive 50 percent of shares they applied for. Bank offered subscription in bond offer worth 40 million pounds over six years with fixed interest of 10.5 percent.

-- National Investment Bank offered investors at least 500,000 shares or 7.14 percent of its holding in partly privatised Alexandria National Iron and Steel (ANSDK). The bank said the offer would open on Tuesday May 27 and close on Monday June 2. Investors can bid for the shares from a floor price of 260.78 pounds, the stock's closing price on the bourse on Thursday.

-- Abu Qir-3 project is considered the most important project undertaken by Abu Qir Fertilisers and Chemical Industries and the largest such scheme in fertilising industry in Egypt. Project costs one billion pounds which will be raised by available liquidity and by increasing capital through closed subscription to senior shareholders.

Company official said project was launched in April and is expected to raise revenue to 1.1 billion pounds. He says project's net profit expected to be about 120 million pounds a year, taking company's net profit to 350 million pounds a year.
